name: Meridian Munitions Twin PDW MTP-2 'Gemini'
description:
The MTP-2 Gemini is a paired weapon system — two identical micro-PDWs sold as a matched set and designed to be dual-wielded with BCI coordination. Each unit is a compact 5.7mm caseless PDW with a 15-round magazine, but the weapons' BCI systems communicate to create a unified fire-control solution. When both weapons are drawn, the smart-link allocates targeting between left and right hands, allowing the operator to engage two separate targets simultaneously.

Dual-wielding weapons is generally impractical — human neurology isn't optimized for independent bilateral targeting. The Gemini's BCI system compensates by handling the targeting math neurally, splitting the operator's attention between two aim points and providing independent aim-assist to each hand. The system requires extensive training and a Class 4 motor-interface BCI, but trained Gemini operators can engage two targets in different directions with the speed of a single-weapon draw.

At Φ8,000 per pair, the Gemini is a specialist system for operators with the neural hardware and training to exploit its capabilities. In untrained hands, the paired weapons offer no advantage over a single PDW with a larger magazine. In trained hands, the Gemini doubles the operator's engagement capacity at close range.
specifications:
caliber: 5.7mm caseless
effective_range: 75m per unit
rate_of_fire: 850 rpm per unit (cyclic)
magazine_capacity: 15 rounds per unit (30 total)
weight: 1.1 kg per unit (2.2 kg total)
tactical_use: The Gemini enables simultaneous multi-target engagement at close range. Trained operators can neutralize two threats in the time it takes a single-weapon operator to engage one. The paired system excels in close-protection scenarios where threats may approach from multiple directions simultaneously. The bilateral targeting AI handles the coordination that human neurology cannot naturally perform, making practical what would otherwise be cinematic fantasy.
cultural_context: The Gemini occupies a strange space between practical weapon and performance art. Dual-wielding has been cinematic fantasy for centuries, and the Gemini makes it functional reality through neural technology. Gemini operators attract attention — the sight of someone drawing and firing two weapons simultaneously is viscerally impressive. This visibility cuts both ways: in covert operations, the distinctive dual-draw is a signature that identifies the operator's equipment and capability.
story_hooks: A Gemini operator's BCI link to one weapon was severed mid-engagement, causing them to fire wildly with their off-hand while maintaining precision with their dominant hand. The split-second of uncontrolled fire hit a bystander.

An underground fighting circuit features Gemini operators in duels — the first competitor to score hits with both weapons simultaneously wins. The matches are illegal, broadcast, and enormously popular.

physical_description.visual_profile: Two identical compact PDWs with aggressive, angular lines and a distinctly asymmetrical grip design. Each weapon features a prominent neural-link receptor on the receiver rail and a minimalist profile optimized for concealment. The silhouette screams precision over bulk—sleek, purposeful, predatory.
physical_description.dimensions: Each unit: 28cm overall length, 6.5cm width at widest point (grip), 5cm height. Barrel length: 12cm. Magazine well sits flush with the frame.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light—1.1kg per unit feels almost insubstantial in hand until you realize the mass is concentrated in the receiver and barrel. Perfectly balanced for dual-wielding; minimal fatigue during sustained fire.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite frame (polymer-ceramic matrix) with chromium-steel barrel and receiver. Structural polymer resists shock and heat cycling.
physical_description.finish: Matte tactical black on the frame with brushed gunmetal accents on the barrel shroud and receiver. The neural-link receptor features a polished titanium contact plate that catches light.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: deep matte black. Accents: brushed gunmetal grey and polished titanium silver at the BCI receptor. Subtle neon-blue underglow along the magazine well (power indicator).
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer with fine crosshatch texture—designed for secure purchase even with chrome-plated fingers. The neural interface grip has micro-tactile feedback nodes that transmit targeting data through haptic feedback.
distinctive_features: Paired neural-link receptors on each receiver (silver contact plates with faint blue LED rings)
Dual aim-assist reticle emitters on the top rail (visible as small crystalline lenses)
Flush, integrated magazine well with witness holes showing round count
Minimal muzzle rise compensation—compensator vents run along the barrel shroud
Ambidextrous controls with identical left/right mirror geometry
Firing selector marked: SAFE | SINGLE | BURST (BCI-COORD) | AUTO
Cross-link status indicator strip along the slide (blue when synced, red when desync)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: MERIDIAN MUNITIONS logo stamped in relief on both sides of the receiver, just forward of the trigger guard. Serial numbers engraved on the barrel (one per unit, but paired numbers—e.g., MTP-2-2226-A and MTP-2-2226-B). Meridian's stylized Φ symbol appears on the grip safety.
physical_description.condition_typical: Typically field-maintained with minor wear on grip surfaces and muzzle edges. The neural-link receptors are kept meticulously clean (contact corrosion degrades BCI signal). Operators often customize with combat tape on the grips or proprietary rail accessories.
